title: What happens when a bracket with a minus sign is opened?
description: A shop rents chairs and tables and gives some money back on return, so the amount paid is one bracket taken from another. The second bracket is opened with both signs changed, and like terms are grouped. Keeko's doubt is that the amount is thirty four x plus eighty five y.
teaching_notes: One idea: a minus sign before a bracket takes away everything inside it, so every sign inside changes when the bracket is opened. Watch for students who change only the first sign inside the bracket.

source: A shop charges 40 rupees per chair and 75 rupees per table,
video_script.why: A learner sees why a minus sign before a bracket changes every sign inside it.
video_script.substitution: the book's shop that rents out chairs and tables and returns some money, checked with x and y as one
video_script.anchor: the rent table of the book, with forty and seventy five rupees paid and six and ten rupees returned
video_script.wrong_answer: thirty four x plus eighty five y
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko changes only the first sign inside the second bracket and leaves the other sign alone. The minus takes away both terms, so the idea is broken with x and y as one.
video_script.payoff_line: The amount paid is thirty four x plus sixty five y rupees

final_answer.value: 34x + 65y rupees; yes, (40x + 75y) + (-6x - 10y) gives the same expression
final_answer.spoken: thirty four x plus sixty five y rupees, and yes, the other way gives the same expression

maths_rules: Keeko test with x = 1, y = 1: 34 + 85 = 119, which is not 99
video_script.design: The rent table stays on the board; the amount is written as one bracket taken from another, the second bracket is opened with both signs changed, and like terms are grouped.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a table with chair 40 and table 75 paid, chair 6 and table 10 returned

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the rent table is drawn
marks.paid: 40 and 75 are written in the paid column
marks.back: 6 and 10 are written in the returned column
marks.ask: a question mark appears under the table

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a shop question from your book.
<bookmark mark='paid'/>The shop rents out chairs and tables. One first pays forty rupees for a chair and seventy five for a table.
<bookmark mark='back'/>On return, the shop gives back six rupees for a chair and ten for a table.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book wants the total paid for x chairs and y tables. What will the expression look like?

beats.on_screen: the rent table stays on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.take: ten counters appear and a bracket of three and two is marked
marks.both: both three and two are taken away

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Take away three plus two from ten counters.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both the three and the two are taken away.
<bookmark mark='write'/>Ten minus three minus two is five. The minus sign acted on everything in the bracket.

beats.on_screen: Given: x chairs and y tables; paid 40 and 75 each; returned 6 and 10 each
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, x chairs and y tables, with the rupees paid and the rupees returned for each.

beats.on_screen: To find: the amount paid in rupees, in its simplest form

marks.find: the words amount paid are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the amount paid in rupees, as short as it can go.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, paid at the start 40x + 75y; returned 6x + 10y; amount paid = (40x + 75y) − (6x + 10y)

marks.paid: 40x + 75y is written for the amount paid at the start
marks.back: 6x + 10y is written for the amount returned

narration: <bookmark mark='paid'/>Step one, the amount paid at the start is forty x plus seventy five y.
<bookmark mark='back'/>The amount returned is six x plus ten y.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The amount paid is the first bracket minus the second bracket.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, open the second bracket and change both signs: 40x + 75y − 6x − 10y

marks.open: the second bracket opens and both of its signs flip

narration: <bookmark mark='open'/>Step two, open the second bracket, because the minus takes away both of its terms.
<bookmark mark='line'/>That gives forty x plus seventy five y minus six x minus ten y.

marks.group: the x terms and the y terms are grouped in two colours

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step three, group the like terms, because terms can be added in any order.
<bookmark mark='bracket'/>Forty x minus six x, and seventy five y minus ten y.
<bookmark mark='short'/>That is forty minus six times x, plus seventy five minus ten times y. The result is thirty four x plus sixty five y.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check with x = 1, y = 1: (40 + 75) − (6 + 10) = 115 − 16 = 99 and 34 + 65 = 99; (40x + 75y) + (−6x − 10y) opens to the same expression

marks.talk: (40x + 75y) + (−6x − 10y) is written and opens to the same line

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check with x and y as one.
<bookmark mark='both'/>One hundred and fifteen minus sixteen is ninety nine. Thirty four plus sixty five is also ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='talk'/>Adding the bracket with minus six x and minus ten y opens to the same expression.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 34x + 65y rupees; yes, (40x + 75y) + (−6x − 10y) gives the same expression
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The amount paid is thirty four x plus sixty five y rupees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the table
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 34x + 85y, struck out; the test x = 1, y = 1 gives 99 and 119

marks.gap: 99 and 119 appear side by side and do not match
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 34x + 65y stays

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the amount is thirty four x plus eighty five y. Keeko changed only the first sign in the bracket.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try x and y as one.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The shop takes one hundred and fifteen and gives back sixteen. That leaves ninety nine, but this idea gives one hundred and nineteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The minus takes away both terms, so both signs change.
